newsitem.title: CROATIA: Largest Croatian oilfield reaches pre-war output.
newsitem.headline: Largest Croatian oilfield reaches pre-war output.

text.p: Croatia's largest oilfield Djeletovci, situated in the Serb-populated Eastern Slavonia enclave, has reached its pre-war production level after almost six years of stagnation, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Djeletovci now produces up to 380 tonnes of oil per day, which is the level we had in 1990, before the war," the spokesman for state-oil monopoly INA told Reuters. That is 18 percent more than we planned at first, he added.
Serbs opposing Croatia's independence from federal Yugoslavia captured Djeletovci in 1991 and continued operating it at a less than optimal rate.
Eastern Slavonia is now reverting to Croatian rule and INA has reopened 14 out of 16 petrol stations in the area.
"After everything is consolidated (in the area) we shall launch new research drilling and start modernising the oilfield," the spokesman said.

Croatia still imports up to two-thirds of its oil. INA and Italian Agip last year started a joint exploration project for gas in the Adriatic Sea, which lies between the two countries. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
